meta.title: Siaya County: ten-year fiscal history

meta.note: Each year is read from the Controller of Budget annual county report for that year. Where two reports give different values for the same year, both are kept in 'alternates'.

FY2023/24: budget, spending and pending bills not yet extracted into this file; own-source revenue is in data/siaya.json.

years.caveat: Comparative figures quoted in the FY2014/15 report. The FY2013/14 report itself has not been read, so the approved budget and pending bills for this year are missing. This was the first year of devolution.

Pending bills of KSh 800.34m are development bills only: the county had not worked out a recurrent figure when the report was written, so no total is plotted. The FY2015/16 report quotes absorption of 78.8 and 59.8 per cent for this year; we use this year's own report. Budget parts add to 5.88 against the stated 5.89.

Page images were read with optical character recognition (the PDF has no text layer). Budget financing shows a local revenue target of KSh 434.91m while the revenue-stream table totals KSh 343.31m; we use the table total with the report's 37.3 per cent. Budget parts add to 6.94 against the stated 6.95.
The report text says recurrent spending was KSh 3.9bn in one sentence and KSh 3.65bn in its table. We use the table, which adds to the KSh 5.63bn total.
Budget components are rounded in the report and add to 8.45.

The report prints KSh 434.38m for both FY2021/22 and FY2020/21 in one sentence; the stated 30.5 per cent rise only works against KSh 332.88m, which is the FY2020/21 figure we use. The same report gives pending bills at 30 June 2021 as KSh 602.08m, against KSh 1,060.92m in the FY2020/21 report; the reports do not explain the difference, so both are shown.

Own-source revenue here excludes KSh 105.81m of appropriations-in-aid; including it the report's total is KSh 508.04m. Pending bills at 30 June 2023 (KSh 761.29m) are the opening stock quoted in the FY2023/24 report; the Auditor-General reports KSh 741.56m. The FY2023/24 report also quotes the FY2022/23 approved budget as KSh 8.50bn, against KSh 8.60bn in the FY2022/23 report.

The scanned text of the recurrent budget is garbled; 5.91 is the approved total minus the development budget. On that figure recurrent absorption is 87.0 per cent, against the report's 85.8 per cent. The FY2024/25 report gives a different own-source revenue for this year (KSh 427.95m); see data/siaya.json. Pending bills: the FY2023/24 report gives KSh 303.91m outstanding at 30 June 2024 but says this excludes bills incurred in the year. The FY2024/25 report gives the stock at 30 June 2024 as KSh 1.12bn, which is the figure used here.

Figures are read from a scanned PDF with two OCR engines (see data/siaya.json). The report states 83 per cent recurrent absorption, but 4.99 of 6.07 is 82.2 per cent. Pending bills at 30 June 2025 could not be read reliably and are not shown. Own-source revenue includes health facility financing.

health.label: Health in Siaya: Kenya Demographic and Health Surveys 2014 and 2022
health.note: The surveys are the only county-level health series that cover ten years. They are samples, so county values carry a margin of error; small changes should not be over-read. Annual routine health data were not retrievable.

indicators.label: Births in a health facility
indicators.note: The county plan reports 98 per cent for facility deliveries, which is probably routine health-system data. The two measures are not the same; we show the survey figure.

Antenatal care from a skilled provider

hiv.label: Adult HIV prevalence, Siaya (per cent of ages 15 to 49)
hiv.warning: The National AIDS Control Council says estimates from different model vintages are not directly comparable. Most of the fall from the 2015 estimate to the 2025 estimate reflects re-modelling, not a measured drop. Do not read these as a trend.

poverty.label: Poverty in Siaya
poverty.note: Two official sources give different monetary poverty rates for 2015/16 and we could not establish why, so both are shown. The multidimensional measure counts people lacking several basic needs at once and is not comparable with the monetary rate.

by_sub_county_2009.note: Sub-counties match constituencies. The six values add to the county total of 842,304. The Siaya CIDP 2018-2022 gives different splits for Ugenya (108,934) and Ugunja (93,372) from ward sums, but the two together are 202,306 either way, so compare the pair when measuring growth.
